title: Chimichurri Sauce
subtitle: Argentinian herb and vinegar sauce for grilled meats
excerpt: Chimichurri is the sauce of the Argentinian asado. It is bright, garlicky, and herb-heavy, made in minutes in a food processor. Pour it over steak, grilled chicken, or anything that has come off the grill.
sourceNotes: Chimichurri is Argentina's defining condiment, used as both a marinade and a table sauce at every asado. The name's origin is debated; the sauce itself is not.

recipe.batchNotes: Make a large batch and store in a jar in the fridge for up to 5 days. The flavour develops over time.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make at least 30 minutes ahead so the flavours have time to come together.

content.text: Pulse the food processor rather than running it continuously. The texture should be finely chopped and slightly chunky, not a smooth paste. If you do not have a food processor, chop everything very finely by hand.
Put the parsley, garlic, and chilli in the food processor. Pulse 5 to 6 times until finely chopped. Do not over-process.
Add the red wine vinegar and dried oregano. Pulse twice more to combine.
Transfer to a bowl or jar. Stir in the olive oil. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Taste: it should be sharp, garlicky, herby, and slightly spicy. Adjust with more vinegar, chilli, or salt.
Leave to rest for at least 30 minutes before serving. Serve at room temperature.

items.symptom: The sauce is paste-like and smooth rather than textured.
items.cause: The food processor was run continuously instead of pulsed.
items.fix: The texture is still fine for marinating; use it chunky next time.

items.cause: Parsley stems were included or the garlic is old.
items.fix: Use tender stems only; replace garlic if it has a green shoot inside.

items.symptom: The sauce has separated and looks oily.
items.cause: Normal separation when left to rest.
items.fix: Stir well before serving; this does not affect the flavour.
